partner_applied.application: After conditioning a curvature vertex cover K, the surviving leaf block is diagonal. Frame deletion gives rho_I det(G_I)>=(1-theta-2q)det(G), so the partner r=0 theorem yields the new density bound. On the m=8 three-hyperbolic-star family this gives ||p_Q||inf<3.544.

new_claims.statement: For two physical hubs with leaf cross Gram G, if K is a vertex cover of leaf off-diagonal curvature, theta=sum_{K}p_i and q=max_{L\K}p_i satisfy theta+2q<1, then Q has a continuous density with ||p_Q||inf<=2sqrt(e)[(1-theta-2q)det G]^(-1/4).
For arbitrary weighted star leaf curvature centered at s, the same bound holds with theta=p_s whenever p_s+2q<1; all star weights, hub core and outside coefficients are arbitrary.

next_step: Threshold the arbitrary leaf curvature. If no low-leverage vertex cover exists, convert the surviving weighted matching/dense curvature into a quantitative cross-volume/tail or ridge certificate, controlling cancellation at singular-value/volume level.
